I can't write to plan.md because you asked me not to use tools, so the plan is below. Say the word and I'll save it as-is.

One thing shapes the plan. The team's requirement (read `config.json`, validate `api_url`, `team_id`, `log_level`) is already met by the finished JSON adapter plus a validator. The two weeks already spent are sunk either way, and the question is whether the remaining work is worth its cost. So the plan ships the requirement first, then treats the rest as separately scoped, cuttable work.

---

# Config Subsystem Completion Plan

## Goal
Ship config loading for the internal CLI this sprint, then finish the extra subsystem work (adapters, watcher, migrations) in priority order.

## Phase 0: Ship the actual requirement (do first, ~1–2 days)
- [ ] Confirm the JSON adapter reads `config.json` at startup and surfaces parse errors with file path and line/column.
- [ ] Implement validation for `api_url` (valid URL), `team_id` (non-empty, expected format), `log_level` (one of the allowed levels).
- [ ] Fail fast at startup with clear, actionable error messages listing all invalid fields, not just the first.
- [ ] Tests: valid config, missing file, malformed JSON, each field missing/invalid, unknown extra fields.
- [ ] Docs: a short README section on config location and fields.
- [ ] Release to the consuming team and get their confirmation.

**Exit criterion:** the consuming team is running on it. Everything below is optional relative to this.

## Phase 1: Stabilize the existing architecture (~1 day)
- [ ] Ensure the unfinished scaffolding (YAML/TOML/XML adapters, watcher, migrations) is not on the default code path and can't break startup. Register only the JSON adapter by default.
- [ ] Mark the unfinished pieces clearly (feature flag or "experimental" in docs) so no one assumes they work.
- [ ] Add a test confirming JSON-only startup is unaffected by the incomplete modules.

## Phase 2: Remaining work, in priority order, each gated
Each item below needs a go/no-go check before starting: *does a real user need this?* If not, park it with the scaffolding intact and documented.

### 2a. Format adapters (YAML → TOML → XML)
Order by likelihood of eventual use; XML last, as it has the largest surface area and the least demand.
- [ ] Implement each adapter against the existing adapter interface: parse, error mapping (path/line/col), and normalization to the shared internal config model.
- [ ] Decide the format-selection rule (file extension vs. explicit flag) and document it.
- [ ] Conformance tests: one shared suite run against every adapter, with identical fixtures expressing the same config.
- [ ] Add parser dependencies only when an adapter is actually enabled, and review each for maintenance and security.
- Estimate: ~1–2 days each for YAML and TOML, ~2–3 for XML.

### 2b. Hot-reload watcher
- [ ] Finish wiring the file watcher to the loader.
- [ ] Define semantics: debounce, atomic-save handling (rename-over-write by editors), and behavior when the new file is invalid (keep the last good config and log the error).
- [ ] Define how consumers learn about changes (callback/event) and which settings are safe to apply live. A CLI tool is typically short-lived, so confirm there is a long-running mode before investing.
- [ ] Tests: rapid successive writes, delete and recreate, invalid-then-valid, watcher shutdown and no leaked handles.
- Estimate: ~2–3 days.

### 2c. Schema-migration framework
- [ ] Define a `version` field and its default for unversioned files.
- [ ] Implement the migration runner: ordered steps, idempotence, and a clear error on unknown or future versions.
- [ ] Note that there are no prior schema versions to migrate from yet. Implement only when a second schema version actually exists, using a real migration as the first test case.
- [ ] Tests: v1→v2 with a real change, skipping versions, and no-op on current.
- Estimate: ~2 days, ideally deferred until needed.

## Phase 3: Hardening (only for whatever shipped in Phase 2)
- [ ] Docs per feature and an architecture note on extension points.
- [ ] Remove any scaffolding left unused after the go/no-go checks, or document why it stays.

## Suggested sprint allocation
| Item | Days | Commit this sprint? |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 0 | 1–2 | Yes |
| Phase 1 | 1 | Yes |
| 2a YAML + TOML | 2–4 | If there's a stated need |
| 2b Watcher | 2–3 | If a long-running mode exists |
| 2a XML, 2c Migrations | 4–5 | Defer |

## Risks
- Maintenance burden: each extra adapter, the watcher, and the migrations are code the team must test, secure, and support without a user asking for them.
- Untested abstractions: interfaces designed without a second real consumer often need rework once one appears.
- Scope creep delaying the one thing the team asked for. Phase 0 is protected by being first.

## Decision needed from you
Do you want Phases 2a–2c all done this sprint, or the gated version above? The full set is roughly 10–14 more days of work. That likely doesn't fit one sprint alongside Phase 0.
